## Combine and inspect tools (`pd-combine`, `pd-inspect`) {#sec-ch14-tools}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: two command-line tools installed with the Python package. `pd-combine` concatenates a run's combined NetCDF
frames along time and merges output streams; `pd-inspect` lists the tensors in a `.part` or `.restart` file.
**Switch**: command line. **Default**: n/a. **Requires**: NCO's `ncrcat` and `ncks` on the `PATH` for `pd-combine`.
**Order**: n/a. **Defining equation**: none.
:::

Both are entry points of the `snapy` package (`[project.scripts]`,
[`pyproject.toml:52-54`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/pyproject.toml#L52-L54)).

### Derivation

None.

### Numerical method

**`pd-combine <ids> [-d dir] [-o name] [--no-remove] [--no-merge]`.** `ParseOutputFields` globs
`*.out*.<5 digits>.nc` in the directory and splits each name into case, stream and stamp
(`ParseOutputFields`, [`pd_combine.py:43-59`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/python/api/pd_combine.py#L43-L59)). For each case and stream, `CombineTimeseries` runs
`ncrcat` over the stamps into `<case>.out<n>.nc`, or renames a single stamp. Unless `--no-remove`, it then deletes the
per-stamp files (`CombineTimeseries`, [`pd_combine.py:6-23`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/python/api/pd_combine.py#L6-L23)). Unless `--no-merge`, `CombineFields`
appends the listed streams into the first with `ncks -A` and moves the result to `<case>-<name>.nc`
(`CombineFields`, [`pd_combine.py:26-40`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/python/api/pd_combine.py#L26-L40)). `main` checks that each requested id exists and also
calls `CombineFITS` for FITS outputs ([`pd_combine.py:82-125`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/python/api/pd_combine.py#L82-L125)).

`pd-combine` does not join blocks in space. A per-block file `<basename>.block<r>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc` (left by
`combine: false`) also matches the glob, with case `<basename>.block<r>`, so each block's frames are concatenated in
time on their own. Joining blocks is done by the run itself (@sec-ch14-netcdf).

**`pd-inspect <paths>`.** For each path, `inspect_path` checks for the bundle magic. For a bundle it prints the
tensors of every part (name, shape, dtype); otherwise it reads the file as one part
(`inspect_path`, [`pd_inspect.py:138-150`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/python/api/pd_inspect.py#L138-L150)).

### Tests

No ctest tests either tool on its own. The `FULL_TESTS` decomposition runners call `pd-combine 0 -o main` on each
case: `run_shallow_splash_decomp.py` skips (exit 125) without it, and `run_shallow_xy_decomp.py` fails without it
(`pd_combine`, [`run_shallow_xy_decomp.py:93-95`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/run_shallow_xy_decomp.py#L93-L95)). `pd-inspect` is used by no test.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `pd-combine` globs every matching `*.out*.nc` in the directory, leftovers included; run it in a clean directory.
- It needs NCO on the `PATH` and deletes its inputs by default.
- It does not join per-block files in space.
:::
